correctness.rationale: For each positive output \(x=p^a m\) with \(p\nmid m\), a preimage \(y=t p^k\) and the factorization \(k=d p^b\) give the exact equations \(a+1=d p^b+b\) and \(m=td\). The map \(b\mapsto d p^b+b\) is strictly increasing, so each permitted divisor \(d\mid m\) produces exactly one positive preimage. All permitted divisors are coprime to \(p\); therefore Chinese-remainder residue counting modulo their least common multiple gives an exact local inverse-multiplicity distribution. The omitted valuation tail has density at most \(p^{-A}\), which proves existence and effective error bounds for every global fiber density. Exact lcm inclusion--exclusion gives the image density without assuming independence. At valuations \(a\le p-2\) the sole divisor is \(a+1\), yielding the logarithmic comparison with rigorously bounded error \(p^{1-p}\). The zero-preimage fiber has a positive valuation cylinder, while the published Emmons--Xiao Theorem 21 supplies a witness for every positive inverse-count level, upgraded to a positive-density periodic cylinder by the new argument. The symbolic proof covers all prime parameters and positive integers; the actual standard-library checker independently reproduces rational finite cutoffs, output membership and inverse multiplicities.

originality.rationale: The earlier Emmons--Xiao Lemma 14 and Theorem 17 describe inverse solutions for fixed x, and Theorem 21 constructs infinitely many x with any prescribed positive finite inverse count. Those statements do not imply the exact natural density of each inverse-count fiber without a new uniform residue-class counting and valuation-tail argument. Their 2023 sequel treats p-adic/number fields and the images of logarithmic derivatives of fields, not ordinary density of the image of integer \(D_p\). Comparable searched published number-theory findings involve different arithmetic functions or full D. No checked complete relevant primary source stated an implication-equivalent density series, verified tail or large-prime law. Unindexed equivalent distribution arguments remain a genuine bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent probabilistic counting argument or overlooked full-text extension may exist, despite source/alias queries and relevant primary comparisons.
The 2012 and 2017 related documents were not exhaustively inspected, so the assessment for them is limited to the material actually read.

value.rationale: The density of an arithmetic function's image is an intrinsic measure of solvability of its defining equation; the full inverse-count probability distribution is likewise a natural invariant directly motivated by the source's finite-fiber and existence problems. The theorem determines all natural densities as explicitly computable infinite sums of rational local data, proves positive mass for every multiplicity, gives rigorous arbitrarily precise numerical intervals, and identifies a universal logarithmic approximation with exponentially small error in the prime. This makes a genuinely new quantitative distributional conclusion, not an isolated case, routine numerical enumeration or table reproduction.
